method.label: Use the altitude and angle bisector

annotationRationale: Pythagorean equations locate the altitude foot and determine squared lengths. The angle-bisector side ratio determines how P divides the altitude.
sourceMethod: Follows the second official solution, omitting its unused preliminary calculation on AC. A signed distance justifies the altitude foot’s location without relying on the official diagram.

review.mathCheck: Subtracting the right-triangle equations gives \(BE=35/2\), placing E inside AB, and \(CE^2=6875/4\). The internal bisector gives \(CP:PE=18:7\), hence \(PE^2=539/4\). Therefore \(BP^2=(1225+539)/4=441\), so BP=21, choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: An originally worded, faithful adaptation of official solution 16's second approach, pp. 12–13. It correctly omits the unused AD/CD calculation and establishes the foot's location explicitly. Its incidences agree with the official figure.
review.annotationCheck: Pythagorean lengths and the angle-bisector side ratio are correctly assessed. Altitude and angle-bisector definitions provide appropriate background. The explanation supplies all geometry needed without the source figure.
